cards.explanation: The answer is False. Moses says the LORD told him, “You shall not cross the Jordan.” He's a hundred and twenty and no longer able to come and go. I think that's a tough thing to say out loud to a whole nation, friends.

The answer is Joshua. Moses says, “Joshua will cross ahead of you, as the LORD has said.” Joshua is the man Moses is about to call up in front of everybody. The LORD goes first, and Joshua goes ahead of the people.

The answer is False. Moses says the LORD will deliver them over, and then Israel must do to them “…exactly as I have commanded you.” There's no room for doing it their own way. It's like a recipe card, friends. You follow it, you don't remix it.

The answer is that the LORD their God goes with them. Moses says, “…it is the LORD your God who goes with you; He will never leave you nor forsake you.” That's the whole reason he gives. Their courage isn't resting on their own strength.

The answer is inheritance. Moses says the land is the one the LORD swore to their fathers, and Joshua will give it to the people as an inheritance. That's something handed down, and here it rests on what the LORD swore. Joshua's job is to go with the people and give it to them, and the LORD Himself goes before him (Deuteronomy 31:8).

The answer is the priests and the elders of Israel. Moses gave the law to “…the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.” That's two groups holding it, not just one person. Me, I'd be nervous with only one keeper, friends, because my hands are a mustache and I once dropped a whole tray of dough with them.

The answer is to read this law out loud. Moses says, “…you are to read this law in the hearing of all Israel.” Every seven years, the whole gathering hears it. That's a lot of folks, so I hope somebody warmed up their voice.

The answer is the foreigners living among them. Moses says to assemble “…men, women, children, and the foreigners within your gates…” The reading isn't just for the folks born in the camp. Everybody gets a seat.

The answer is follow. Moses wants them to listen and learn “…to fear the LORD your God and to follow carefully all the words of this law.” Hearing it is only step one, friends. Following it is where it lands.

The answer is True. Moses says their children who don't know the law will listen and learn to fear the LORD your God, “…as long as you live in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.” The reading in verse 12 gathers everyone: men, women, children, and the foreigners within your gates. So the children aren't left out of the room. They're right there in the crowd, listening.

The answer is commission. The LORD says, “Call Joshua and present yourselves at the Tent of Meeting, so that I may commission him.” Moses isn't doing the commissioning here. The LORD is, and Moses walks Joshua there.

The answer is that they will turn to foreign gods and break His covenant. The LORD says they “…will rise up and prostitute themselves with the foreign gods of the land they are entering.” Then He says, “They will forsake Me and break the covenant I have made with them.” This is a hard word to hear, friends.

The answer is that they'll ask if it's because their God isn't with them. The LORD says they will say, “Have not these disasters come upon us because our God is no longer with us?” It's a question they ask when the troubles pile up. I think that one carries a lot of ache.
The answer is True. The LORD says, “…on that day I will surely hide My face because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods.” He names the reason Himself. It's a serious line.

The answer is that the song is a witness for Him against them. The LORD has Moses write the song down and teach it to the Israelites so it stands as a witness for Him against them. Then He says it “…will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants.” So this song is meant to be sung, and sung for a long time.

The answer is False. The LORD says this song “…will not be forgotten from the lips of their descendants.” So it doesn't fade after one generation. It's meant to be handed down the line. Moses wrote it down and taught it to the Israelites that very day (Deuteronomy 31:22).

The answer is that He knows it before they enter the land. The LORD says, “…I know their inclination, even before I bring them into the land that I swore to give them.” He isn't waiting to find out. He already knows.

The answer is True. The LORD says to Joshua, “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land that I swore to give them, and I will be with you.” It's the same call Moses gave him. This time it comes straight from the LORD, with a promise attached.

The answer is beside the ark of the covenant. Moses says, “Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God…” It stays there “…as a witness against you.” The Levites who carry the ark are the ones he tells.

The answer is False. Moses says, “If you are already rebelling against the LORD while I am still alive, how much more will you rebel after my death!” That's his honest warning, friends. It's a heavy one.

The answer is the elders and officers of the tribes. Moses says, “Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officers…” He wants them in front of him so he can speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them. So the room he asks for is Israel's own leaders, tribe by tribe. These are heavy words, and he wants those leaders there to hear them.

The answer is the path he commanded them. Moses says, “…after my death you will become utterly corrupt and turn from the path I have commanded you.” The path is the one he gave them. I think those are heavy words to say to people he has led. He adds that in the days to come, disaster will befall them because they will do evil in the sight of the LORD.

The answer is disaster. Moses says, “…in the days to come, disaster will befall you because you will do evil in the sight of the LORD…” It's a heavy ending to this stretch of his speech, so I'll just say it plainly.
